head: faecalibacterium
notes: MR-protective for coronary atherosclerosis (IVW OR=0.84, p=0.01, MiBioGen+FinnGen); butyrate → HDAC inhibition → anti-inflammatory → anti-atherogenic; Faecalibacterium depletion is one of the most replicated findings in CVD microbiome studies

head: akkermansia
notes: MR-protective for atherosclerosis; Amuc_1100 → TLR2 → barrier → reduced LPS → reduced endothelial activation → reduced atherogenesis; Akkermansia depletion is consistent across ACVD cohort metagenomics

head: bifidobacterium
notes: MR-protective for atherosclerosis (MiBioGen+FinnGen IVW); butyrate/acetate → barrier/anti-inflammatory → anti-atherogenic; FUT2-instrumental variable MR confirms causal direction

head: desulfovibrio
notes: MR-protective for coronary and peripheral atherosclerosis (IVW OR=0.89, p=0.048); H2S → KATP channel → vasodilation → anti-atherogenic at physiological concentrations; consistent across MR sensitivity analyses

head: ruminococcaceae_ucg010
notes: MR-protective for coronary (OR=0.80, p=0.006) AND peripheral atherosclerosis (OR=0.65, p=0.013); strongest MR signal in the Gut Microbiome–CVD MR literature; butyrate production mechanism

head: faecalibacterium
notes: MR-protective for T2D (IVW OR=0.87, p=0.02, MiBioGen+DIAGRAM); butyrate → GPR109A/GPR43 → improved insulin sensitivity; Faecalibacterium prausnitzii is the most replicated protective taxon in T2D microbiome

head: oscillospira
notes: MR-protective for T2D (IVW OR<1, p<0.05, MiBioGen+DIAGRAM); associated with leanness and lower fasting glucose across multiple cohorts; butyrate production mechanism; depleted in obesity and T2D

head: blautia
notes: MR-protective for T2D (MiBioGen+DIAGRAM IVW direction protective); acetate production → GPR43 → improved glucose homeostasis; Blautia depletion is consistent in T2D metagenomics across QinJ/Karlsson/MetaCardis

head: lachnospiraceae_nk4a136
notes: MR-protective for HF and T2D; butyrate producer; depleted in MetaCardis T2D subjects; butyrate → GPR43/GPR109A → insulin sensitivity

head: escherichia
notes: LPS production → metabolic endotoxemia → TLR4 → NF-κB → insulin resistance → T2D; E. coli LPS is the primary driver of metabolic endotoxemia; elevated in T2D across multiple cohorts; MR-risk signal for related metabolic endpoints
